name: Index Packaging, Inc.
old_description: Index Packaging’s manufacturing facility in Milton, New Hampshire specializes in wood packaging products, including wood crates and wood pallets, both new and recycled. Since we control the entire production process and have our own fleet of vehicles serving New England, we can guarantee your order will be on time.
about:
Index Packaging, Inc. operates from Milton, New Hampshire, where it has been based since 1981. The company was founded in 1968 by Bill and Connie Lander in the basement of their New York home and remains a closely held, family‑owned corporation. Leadership passed to their son Bruce Lander in 1997, and the board today includes Bruce as chairman and family shareholders Connie Lander and Debora Lussier.

The firm designs and manufactures custom protective packaging for fragile or high‑value items, working across three material families — foam (polyurethane and polyethylene), wood (crates, pallets, and kiln‑dried lumber compliant with ISPM‑15), and corrugated fiberboard. Four New Hampshire facilities in Milton, Dover, Merrimack, and Somersworth provide roughly 290,000 square feet of combined design, engineering, production, and warehousing space, supported by a workforce of more than 200 employees. Services extend to vendor‑managed inventory, just‑in‑time warehousing, and a dedicated trucking fleet for New England deliveries plus nationwide LTL, FedEx, and UPS shipping.

Customers span industrial equipment manufacturers, military and defense programs, medical, pharmaceutical, and laboratory sectors, and food and agriculture businesses. The company also produces retail‑focused lines such as foam‑filled apple gift shippers for specialty grocery and subscription boxes.

Index Packaging emphasizes its “Protection by Design” philosophy, citing in‑house design and engineering at no cost to qualified buyers, the convenience of foam, wood, and corrugated capabilities under one roof, and the agility of a family‑owned structure that enables quick decision‑making. An in‑house recycling program diverts foam, corrugated, and wood scrap into secondary markets.
